item.author: Lam Ka-sing
item.dc:creator: Lam Ka-sing
item.description: Hongkongers will experience the chilliest days of autumn yet, with temperatures expected to drop to 16 degrees Celsius (61 Fahrenheit) this week as a cold front sweeps across the southern Chinese coast. The expected drop to 16 degrees on Friday and Saturday may mark the coldest days of the month, falling below the previous low of 17.5 degrees recorded in the city on November 10, according to records on the Hong Kong Observatory’s website. Temperatures earlier in the month had remained above 17.5...
item.title: Hongkongers face chilliest days of the season as cold front brings wind and rain

item.dc:creator: Holly Chik
item.description: Chinese ambassador to the United States Xie Feng has signalled high hopes for major-power cooperation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen this week, promoting a China-led AI alliance for regional prosperity. The prosperity theme was also highlighted in Qiushi, the Communist Party’s flagship publication, which compiled a series of President Xi Jinping’s previous Apec speeches on building an “Asia-Pacific community with a shared future”. Since his first Apec meeting...
item.title: China calls for AI cooperation with the US ahead of Shenzhen Apec summit

item.author: Edith Lin
item.dc:creator: Edith Lin
item.description: Hong Kong’s police chief has dismissed concerns that geopolitical tensions could affect attendance at the coming Interpol general assembly to be held in the city, saying transnational cooperation on policing is “inevitable”. item.title: Geopolitics won’t affect Interpol assembly, ‘inevitable’ police cooperation: Joe Chow

item.author: Theodora Yu
item.dc:creator: Theodora Yu
item.description: The charred body of an elderly woman was found in a flat in Hong Kong’s Wong Tai Sin after a blaze broke out on Sunday morning, with officers uncovering a large amount of clutter piled up all the way to the ceiling. The Fire Services Department received a report at 8.45am on Sunday of a No 1 alarm fire at a lower-floor residential flat at Lung Kwong House in Wong Tai Sin. Firefighters arrived a few minutes later and extinguished the fire within 26 minutes, at 9.16am. Some 300 people were...
item.title: Elderly woman found dead after blaze in cluttered Wong Tai Sin flat

item.author: Liu Zhen
item.dc:creator: Liu Zhen
item.description: China has upgraded its VT-4 series main battle tank with cutting-edge technologies aimed at the international market, newly surfaced photos show ahead of the country’s premier defence exhibition in Zhuhai. The appearance of the new tank, believed to be designated as VT-4B, indicates significant upgrades over the existing VT-4A in its armour protection, active protection, weapon station and electronic equipment. Some of the improvements show traits of technologies developed for China’s...
item.title: China’s upgraded VT-4B export tank gets fourth-gen Type 100 tech ahead of Zhuhai show

item.author: Ralph Jennings
item.dc:creator: Ralph Jennings
item.description: Chinese and South Korean shipping through the Arctic Ocean to Europe has increased this year, although unpredictable ice, high costs and lapses in demand have exposed the challenges of navigating the route, an environmental research group has found. During the late summer and early autumn shipping season, delays forced one Chinese operator to extend some journeys from 20 days to 30 days, the Oslo-based Bellona Foundation said in a report. Traffic along the Arctic seaway has been busier than last...
item.title: Sudden ice, high costs: are China’s Arctic shipping ambitions at risk after traffic surge?

item.author: The Korea Times
item.dc:creator: The Korea Times
item.description: The South Korean government said Nvidia’s existing partnership commitments to Seoul remain intact despite disgraced CEO Jensen Huang’s departure from the artificial intelligence giant. However, uncertainties linger as remarks by Elon Musk and others suggest that much of the cooperation may have relied on Huang’s personal verbal commitments. The Ministry of Science and ICT said it held a meeting with Nvidia officials on Friday, a day after Huang resigned as the company’s CEO, and confirmed that...
item.title: South Korea calms fears over 260,000 Nvidia chip order after Jensen Huang’s exit

item.author: Cheryl Arcibal
item.dc:creator: Cheryl Arcibal
item.description: The United Arab Emirates, a favoured destination for foreign property investment, could see support for housing demand and prices if heavy midterm losses for US President Donald Trump’s Republican Party help bring an end to the Iran war, analysts said, adding that housing markets across the wider Middle East could also benefit. Property demand in Abu Dhabi and Dubai, the two largest emirates in the UAE, cooled in recent months, according to data tracked by JLL, following the US-Israel war on...
item.title: Dubai, Abu Dhabi property markets could gain if Trump’s midterm losses help end Iran war

item.author: Leopold Chen
item.dc:creator: Leopold Chen
item.description: Hong Kong police have arrested a taxi driver for alleged dangerous driving after his vehicle hit two British nationals who were crossing the road in Wan Chai. Police said on Sunday that the incident happened at 1.39am, when the victims – a 65-year-old man and a 58-year-old woman – were crossing the road near Hay Wah Building in Wan Chai while the taxi was travelling west along Hennessy Road. The victims sustained head injuries and were admitted to Queen Mary Hospital in Pok Fu Lam. The man was...
item.title: Hong Kong taxi driver arrested after 2 Britons hit by cab in Wan Chai

item.author: Eric Jiang
item.dc:creator: Eric Jiang
item.description: The Victoria Harbour Race on Sunday ended in chaos and disappointment for hundreds of swimmers, after organisers cancelled the final waves of amateur competitors, while reports said others were pulled from the water with the finish line in sight. With the 11.30am cut-off time fast approaching, the fourth batch of leisure swimmers, which had 700 spaces allocated to it, were left on dry land when organisers pulled the plug at 9.25am, some 20 minutes after the waves of the race’s slowest entrants...
item.title: 700 swimmers left stranded after strong currents force early end to Victoria Harbour Race

item.author: Caroline Lin
item.dc:creator: Caroline Lin
item.description: China’s bricks-and-mortar bookstores are increasingly counting on coffee, merchandise and cultural events rather than books to stay afloat – a survival strategy whose tensions were laid bare after a major chain asked a book buyer to vacate its cafe seating unless she bought a drink. The dispute at a Beijing branch of Sisyphe Bookstore, one of the country’s largest chains, went viral earlier this month, sparking an online debate over the struggles bookshops face in the digital age. The customer,...
item.title: What a Beijing cafe dispute reveals about China’s struggling bookshops

item.author: Tribune News Service
item.dc:creator: Tribune News Service
item.description: When Iran’s military planners prepared to hit American bases in the Middle East, they relied on intelligence from an unlikely source: US service members themselves. According to security experts and even the US military, Iran harvested data from social media accounts, fitness apps and even ads to establish patterns of life in US bases across the region. Paired with imagery reportedly provided by Russian satellites, the Iranians selecting the targets constructed a surprisingly accurate picture of...
item.title: How Iran used US troops’ digital footprints to hit Mideast bases for billions in damage

item.author: Theodora Yu
item.dc:creator: Theodora Yu
item.description: Hong Kong must proactively expand trade networks and not “wait for luck to come our way”, as artificial intelligence development that drove recent growth in exports may gradually slow down, the city’s commerce minister has said. Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau Ying-wah said on Sunday that Hong Kong’s September export growth rate – the highest monthly figure in more than 40 years – was driven by an increase in re-export volume equivalent to 1.4 times the city’s gross...
item.title: Hong Kong must expand trade networks as AI development could slow, commerce chief says

item.author: Vincent Tan
item.dc:creator: Vincent Tan
item.description: Malaysia’s plans to allow registered refugees to work legally have raised hopes among their communities that have long relied on precarious informal employment to survive, even as Thailand’s experience suggests that such a move is only part of the solution. Thailand has reportedly thousands of refugees taking up formal jobs under a scheme introduced last year. As for Malaysia’s initiative, refugee advocates say it will need clear registration procedures and workplace safeguards to make it...
item.title: Malaysian plan to let refugees work spurs advocates’ call for safeguards

item.author: Xinyi Wu
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Wu
item.description: China has ushered artificial intelligence into its cinemas, but the country’s first fully AI-generated feature film has flopped at the box office. Made with no human actors or camera crew, Sanxingdui: Future Past brought in just around 1.8 million yuan (US$270,000) after three weeks in theatres, according to Chinese box office data tracker Beacon Pro. The figure was well below the film’s reported budget of tens of millions of yuan. The 100-minute sci-fi film is set in a world decades in the...
item.title: No actors, no crew, no ticket sales: ‘So obviously AI’ film flops at China’s box office

item.author: Edith Lin
item.dc:creator: Edith Lin
item.description: The internationally acclaimed pianist Yuja Wang has denied making a last-minute change to a recent performance in Hong Kong that resulted in audience refunds, saying the concert organiser was told weeks in advance about the revised programme. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Beijing-born American pianist and the Mahler Chamber Orchestra accused the local organiser, Premiere Performances of Hong Kong, of withholding the announcement of a change that had been “communicated weeks in advance by...
item.title: Hong Kong concert organiser told ‘weeks in advance’ about changed programme: Yuja Wang

item.author: Lexi Tian
item.dc:creator: Lexi Tian
item.description: Hong Kong International Airport has become the world’s first to deploy robots to repaint runway markings, cutting the time needed to refresh centre lines by about 67 per cent compared with manual painting, its managing authority has said. According to the Airport Authority, the AI-powered robots, called “Brushman”, also improve painting accuracy and worker safety, reducing the need for physically demanding overnight work and allowing staff to take on supervisory roles. Steven Yiu Siu-chung, the...
item.title: Fresh coat, lighter load: Hong Kong airport puts runway-painting robots to work

item.author: Gabriel Dominguez
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Dominguez
item.description: Before mainland Chinese troops could attempt a landing on Taiwan, they would first have to assemble vehicles, weapons and supplies along the coast – potentially exposing them to Taiwanese drone, rocket and missile attacks. A nighttime drill reported by state broadcaster CCTV on June 11 offered a glimpse of how the People’s Liberation Army could shield those amphibious forces as they prepared to cross the Taiwan Strait. As soldiers headed into open water aboard amphibious armoured vehicles, a...
item.title: Could Beijing’s HQ-17 air-defence system defend PLA amphibious forces from Taiwan strikes?

item.author: David D. Lee
item.dc:creator: David D. Lee
item.description: Alina Radulescu, 38, has stayed in Italy, the United States and Thailand for months at a time. Now, the IT consultant from Romania shares a co-living space in Seoul with 11 other digital nomads – and says she’s never been happier. “There’s a certain vibe in Korea,” she said. “These days, I’m just so happy when I realise that I’m living here.” Her affinity for South Korea grew gradually through friends in Romania and dance classes where her teacher played K-pop. item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: South Korean police said on Sunday they had launched an investigation after the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam confessed to using artificial intelligence to cheat. The test taker, who ranked first in both rounds of the national qualification exam held in April and July, submitted a written confession through his lawyer and acknowledged using AI to obtain answers during the tests. He scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, sparking...
item.title: Top tax accountant exam scorer in South Korea admits to using AI to cheat

item.author: Daisy Wu
item.dc:creator: Daisy Wu
item.description: UBS has drawn back the curtains on its new Hong Kong headquarters in West Kowloon, a 20-storey tower with a client floor built for meetings, dinners and events, as the Swiss lender anchors its regional presence to tap growing wealth across the Greater Bay Area. About 3,500 UBS staff, currently spread across five offices, including Two IFC in Central, are due to start moving in during the fourth quarter. UBS Tower sits within Sun Hung Kai Properties’ International Gateway Centre. It has about...
item.title: UBS unveils new West Kowloon hub to tap Greater Bay Area wealth

item.author: Zoey Zhang
item.dc:creator: Zoey Zhang
item.description: In China, some influential online voices offering health advice are neither doctors nor academics, but AI-generated blue aliens. Depicted as emissaries from an advanced civilisation, the bald, blue-skinned digital figures have humanlike bodies and glowing markings across their heads. The phenomenon reportedly traces its origins to Wanxiang Science, a popular-science channel on Douyin with more than 1.5 million followers. item.title: AI ‘blue aliens’ rising as health experts on China social media spark pseudoscience backlash

item.description: For some ⁠people, the blue, green and white striped socks hanging near the entrance of a FamilyMart convenience store may look more like an emergency purchase than a fashion statement. Yet the 390 yen (US$2.44) socks have become one of Japan’s best-known products at convenience stores, which are usually the go-to for snacks and drinks. With 40 million pairs sold since 2021, they have helped FamilyMart reinvent itself as a lifestyle brand in the competitive conbini market. Now, Japan’s...
item.title: Japan’s FamilyMart pulls up striped socks to survive convenience store rivalry

item.author: Denise Tsang
item.dc:creator: Denise Tsang

item.title: Hong Kong sending who’s who delegation of business leaders to Apec CEO Summit

item.dc:creator: Alcott Wei
item.description: Pseudo-history about China is mushrooming online, spreading fake accounts of the past due in large part to platform algorithms, artificial intelligence (AI) and a lack of monitoring, according to a Chinese provincial authority. item.dc:creator: Chong Ming Lee

Among top officials flying in are Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, Chinese Premier Li Qiang and US President Donald Trump, with the latter expected to attend on Tuesday . item.description: Identity politics could very well decide the outcome of Malaysia’s next national election, experts say, after parties and voters dug in their heels along ethnic lines in recent polls that have undermined Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s multicultural ruling coalition. On Saturday, Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan (PH) suffered its third straight electoral defeat this year in Melaka state as the incumbent Barisan Nasional (BN) coalition and its new partner, the Perikatan Nasional (PN) federal opposition...

item.author: Reuters
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in mid-air by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier. It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for – the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s lift-off from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch. Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless...

item.author: Saimum Parvez
item.dc:creator: Saimum Parvez
item.description: Talks at Cop31, the United Nations climate change conference being held in Antalya, Turkey, come at a critical moment for climate-vulnerable countries across the Global South. Bangladesh is among those bearing the brunt of climate change despite having negligible historical responsibility for global emissions. As delegations negotiate how to finance climate action, the “how” matters no less than the “how much”: support must arrive in time, reach those who need it and avoid deepening debt. The...
item.title: For Bangladesh and others, climate disasters should not add to debt burdens

item.author: Kang Jun-young
item.dc:creator: Kang Jun-young
item.description: The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19. The venue is not accidental. Forty years ago, this was a border town of rice fields and duck ponds; it is now where a good part of the world’s electronics are designed and built, and the showcase of China’s “reform and opening up”. The event’s theme, “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together”, puts openness, innovation and cooperation at the centre. US President Donald Trump...
item.title: Amid the Xi-Trump clamour, can Apec revive the business of cooperation?

item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Weary travellers braced for more flight disruptions on Saturday as service resumed from US airports after an hours-long stoppage that the Trump administration blamed on faulty equipment or an error by a contractor tasked with switching out old copper wire communication lines. Friday’s nationwide ground stop sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before departure by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding...

item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: Filipino singer Carmelle won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest on Saturday with a fiery performance of her dance-pop song “Sobra-Sobra”. The 19-year-old beat 10 other acts in the grand final in Bangkok, with the winner chosen through votes from national juries in participating countries and viewers worldwide. After her victory, Carmelle said her song celebrated female empowerment and was intended as “a tribute to all Filipino women”. “I made history, since this was the first...
item.title: Philippines’ Carmelle storms to victory in Eurovision Asia debut in Bangkok

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.description: US negotiators have floated the idea of Ukraine’s potential withdrawal from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining Nato, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, following the latest round of peace talks with Russia in Abu Dhabi. This is the first time the question of linking Nato membership to territorial concessions has been raised during the talks, Zelensky said in remarks ‌to reporters released by his office on Saturday. “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins Nato?...
item.title: Zelensky says US floated idea of Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership

item.dc:creator: Phoebe Zhang
item.description: Disciplinary staff in Wuhan, provincial capital of Hubei in central China, were going about their routine workday when a red alert landed. item.author: Agence France-Presse
item.dc:creator: Agence France-Presse
item.description: Six people were arrested overnight after a huge blast at a steel plant near the western city of Izmir killed 17 workers, with grieving families waiting on Tuesday to receive their loved ones’ bodies for burial. Onlookers said Monday’s massive explosion felt like “an earthquake” when it ripped through the Habas steel factory in Aliaga, a district 60km (37 miles) north of Izmir known for ship-breaking and heavy industry. item.author: Cannix Yau
item.dc:creator: Cannix Yau
item.description: Hong Kong’s MTR Corporation has warned that it will face significant cash flow pressures over the next few years, even with the government’s grant of eight new sites for developing the Northern Link rail project in the Northern Metropolis. item.title: Hong Kong rail giant warns of cash crunch despite Northern Metropolis land grant

item.dc:creator: Phoebe Zhang,William Zheng
item.description: Drones are banned, security cameras bristle at intersections and some residents have been asked to vacate their homes as the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen counts down to the Apec meetings. item.author: Jess Ma
item.dc:creator: Jess Ma

item.dc:creator: Carol Yang
item.description: China and South Korea have agreed to use next week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen to advance bilateral ties, according to their top diplomats. The pledge by Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his South Korean counterpart Cho Hyun after talks in Beijing on Friday comes as Seoul seeks Beijing’s help to revive stalled dialogue with Pyongyang. item.author: Jess Ma
item.dc:creator: Jess Ma
item.description: Hong Kong residents have been warned about fake vehicle airbag safety recall messages circulating widely on WhatsApp, with the Chinese-language notices bearing the Transport Department’s name. item.title: Fake Toyota airbag recall notices circulating on WhatsApp, Hongkongers warned

item.author: Alice Yan
item.dc:creator: Alice Yan
item.description: In ancient China, when a man became seriously ill, his family might arrange a wedding for him in an attempt to drive away the disease. The custom is called chong xi, literally translated as “clashing with joy”. Its rationale is that a happy event could lift one’s spirits and thereby dispel illness or other misfortunes. In practice, if a man who was already engaged became seriously ill, his family might move his wedding forward. If he did not yet have a fiancée, his family might hastily find him...
item.title: How Chinese custom ‘chong xi,’ or ‘clashing with joy,’ can counteract misfortune

item.author: Shi Huang
item.dc:creator: Shi Huang
item.description: From A-list underwear campaigns to everyday wardrobe staples, tight briefs are often hailed as the ultimate symbol of masculine appeal. However, a major new study out of China suggests that choosing tight underwear over classic boxer shorts could lead to higher rates of erectile dysfunction, premature ejaculation and prostatitis. A snug fit also impairs sperm quality, according to the findings published in the Asian Journal of Andrology last month. Loose underwear may offer a simple alternative...

item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Wang
item.description: China is updating a law that has underpinned one of the most remarkable industrial transformations of our time. item.description: Nearly a year after taking effect, the landmark High Seas Treaty risks becoming another geopolitical battleground among major powers, observers have warned.
